slides.say: Given: x plus three, in absolute value, is smaller than seven. Which of the following could be the value of x?

So now the bars are in an inequality, and they're on the small side. What did we say about the small side? It's a closed range. The inside is trapped between seven and negative seven. [short pause] We'll solve it three ways.

[short pause] Our first method, the algebra. The inside is trapped, so I take the seven, and I put negative seven on the other side. So negative seven is smaller than x plus three, which is smaller than seven.
at: negative seven on the other side

slides.say: How do I get x alone in the middle? I take three off all three parts. Negative seven minus three is negative ten, and seven minus three is four. So x is between negative ten and four.
Now the choices. Five and eleven are too big, they're above four. Negative twenty-five is too small, it's below negative ten. And three is inside the range. So three, number three is our answer.
[pause] Our second method, the number line. x plus three is the distance from negative three. So x is less than seven steps away from negative three.

Seven steps to the left, negative ten. Seven steps to the right, four. One band in the middle, from negative ten to four. Three is inside it. Five and eleven are past four, and negative twenty-five is way past negative ten, so they're outside. Three, number three.
[pause] Our third method, plugging in the answers. Five plus three is eight, not smaller than seven. Negative twenty-five plus three is negative twenty-two, its absolute value is twenty-two. Too big.
Three plus three is six, and six is smaller than seven. It works, so in the exam you circle it and move on.

slides: [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
